title: Get the stones out of a running shoe: tip it opening-down with the toe up, shake all 8 out, set it back down
instruction: There are some small stones in this shoe. Get them all out, then put the shoe back down on the table, sole down.
context: Most people have stopped on a walk or a run to take off a shoe and tip out a stone; left in, it rubs a blister (Advnture, 2023), and about 2.1 billion pairs of footwear were bought in the US in 2024 (World Footwear Yearbook 2025). Everyone does it the same way: hold the shoe by the heel, turn it opening-down with the toe up, shake until the stones drop out, and put it down. Here a men's US 9 road running shoe at full size (297 g) holds eight gravel pebbles of 4 to 8 mm, a graded count: trail gravel often gets in several at once. The insole slopes down to the toe (10 mm drop), so most stones lie in the toe box under the closed upper, 20 cm or more from the opening at the heel. Turned over with the toe still low, they stay there; they leave only when the toe is raised above the opening and the shoe is shaken, and the last one or two catch at the heel and need another shake with the opening straight down. Unlike shaking a counted few mints from a box, the shoe is emptied completely.
setup: Centimetres from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the table top. (1) One men's US 9 road running shoe at true size, modelled on the Nike Pegasus 41: 297 g, 10 mm heel-to-toe drop, 37/27 mm stack, outer length 290 mm, widest 100 mm at the ball, collar opening about 100 x 67 mm (length, width and opening are estimates). Blue upper, white midsole, black outsole, white laces; the upper, tongue and laces are one rigid shell with 4.5 mm walls, closed over the toe box, with a padded heel counter and a rigid heel pull tab, 12 mm thick, 30 mm wide, standing 35 mm above the counter (a real tab is a stiff stitched loop, an estimate; the hand pinches it at the root). It stands on its sole, laces tied, heel counter at (33, -8), heading 60 degrees from x toward the robot's left (toe at about (47, 17)), opening up. (2) Inside it, 8 gravel pebbles, irregular, 4.1 to 8.0 mm long, 0.04 to 0.28 g (quartz-like, 2.65 g/cm3): 4 in the toe box under the vamp, 2 at the midfoot, 2 at the heel, resting on the insole, which slopes down from the heel to the toe. Nothing else is on the table. Layout B (SHOE_LAYOUT=B): the heel counter at (32, -10), heading 50 degrees, the stones in other places in the same three groups. Real trial: any lace-up running shoe of this size with a heel pull tab, and 8 stones sieved from washed pea gravel between 4 and 8 mm sieves, dropped in through the collar and shaken to the toe.
scoring: Scored at the end, by count and by the shoe's pose. A stone is out when it is no longer in the shoe: not within the shoe's outline above its sole (a stone on the collar's lip counts as in; one on the table under the sole's edge as out). 0.25: at least 2 of the 8 out. 0.5: at least 4 out. 0.75: at least 6 out, or all 8 out but the shoe not set down. 1.0: all 8 out and the shoe set down: resting on its sole on the table (insole within 20 degrees of level), both grippers open and every part of both grippers at least 3 cm from the shoe, all held for the last 2 s. Score 0 if the shoe is dropped or thrown (it ever moves faster than 0.45 m/s, a 1 cm fall, with no gripper closed on it) or ends off the table. Picking a stone out with a finger is allowed and counts. Real trial: count the stones on the table, then tip the shoe into a hand to confirm none is left; level checked against a 20 degree card wedge; the hand's clearance and any drop seen in a phone video.
reset_notes: Nothing is random: the shoe and the eight stones start at their marks (layout A); SHOE_LAYOUT=B turns and moves the shoe and changes the stones' places.
fidelity: Rigid bodies at 240 Hz on GPU, CCD on each body and the scene. The shoe is one rigid body (upper, tongue and laces fused): a modelled shell of 141 convex pieces with 4.5 mm walls, true size, 297 g; a real upper flexes a little, which tipping and shaking do not need. Pebbles are irregular convex hulls 4 to 8 mm, mass from volume at 2.65 g/cm3. Estimates: length, collar, pull tab (rigid; a real one is a stiff loop), friction 0.5 to 0.6, no restitution.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; demo: 1.0 (one hand, 624 steps; layout B also 1.0). Lazy routes on GPU: nothing 0; shaken with the opening up 0; opening down with the toe kept low 0 (all 8 stay in the toe box); emptied then rolled onto its side 0 (void); emptied then let go 10 cm up 0 (void).
